rows.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها
rows.claim: They hold that the basmala is not a Qur'anic verse, but was written to separate surahs and for blessing; they therefore do not recite it aloud in prayer.
rows.anchor: قراء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها على ان التسمية ليست بآية من الفاتحة ولا من غيرها من السور وإنما كتبت للفصل والتبرك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ومن تابعه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa shares the view that the basmala is not a verse, and his followers accordingly do not recite it aloud in prayer.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله ومن تابعه ولذلك لا يجهر بها عندهم في الصلاة

rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما
rows.claim: They hold that the basmala is a verse of al-Fatiha and every surah; al-Shafi'i and his companions agree and recite it aloud.
rows.anchor: وقراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما على انها آية من الفاتحة ومن كل سورة وعليه الشافعي وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposing jurists argue that the early community included the basmala in the codex while excluding Amin, so it must be Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقالوا قد أثبتها السلف في المصحف مع توصيتهم بتجريد القرآن ولذلك لم يثبتوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that whoever omits the basmala has omitted 114 verses from God's Book.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس من تركها فقد ترك مائة وأربع عشرة آية من كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi is attached to an omitted verb such as I read or recite in God's name; the reciter supplies the action begun by the basmala.
rows.anchor: بمحذوف تقديره بسم الله اقرأ أو أتلو لأن الذي يتلو التسمية مقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted governing verb is placed after the basmala because God's name, the more important element, should come first and signal exclusive invocation of God.
rows.anchor: لأن الأهم من الفعل والمتعلق به هو المتعلق به لأنهم كانوا يبدءون بأسماء آلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposed divine name conveys exclusivity, as in the explicit object-first wording of You alone we worship.
rows.anchor: فوجب ان يقصد الموحد معنى اختصاص اسم الله عز وجل بالابتداء وذلك بتقديمه وتأخير الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's omitted verb is illustrated by Arabic prayers for a newly married couple and by a poet's account of being called to a meal.
rows.anchor: في الدعاء للمعرس بالرفاء والبنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is supported by Noah's words about embarking and landing in God's name.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بسم الله مجراها ومرساها ﴾ هود 41

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first-revealed surah, placing the command to read before the basmala is more fitting because the reading command is paramount.
rows.anchor: هناك تقديم الفعل اوقع لأنها اول سورة نزلت فكان الامر بالقراءة أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes the name relate to reciting as a pen relates to writing: the believer makes the act God's by beginning with His name, as a prophetic report says.
rows.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لم يبدأ فيه باسم الله فهو أبتر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that an important matter begun without God's name is cut off.
rows.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لم يبدأ فيه باسم الله فهو أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other analysis treats reciting as occurring in the blessing of God's name; al-Zamakhshari calls this account more idiomatic and better.
rows.anchor: على معنى متبركا بسم الله أقرأ وكذلك قول الداعي للمعرس بالرفاه والبنين معناه أعرست ملتبسا بالرفاه والبنين وهذا الوجه أعرب وأحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine basmala and praise on worshippers' tongues teach them how to invoke, praise, glorify, and magnify God.
rows.anchor: ومعناه تعليم عباده كيف يتبركون باسمه وكيف يحمدونه ويمجدونه ويعظمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One-letter particles usually take fatḥa; lām takes kasra to distinguish it from the introductory lām, while bi takes kasra because it is inherently a preposition.
rows.anchor: اما اللام فللفصل بينها وبين لام الابتداء واما الباء فلكونها لازمة للحرفية والجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun ism begins with a consonant cluster, so speakers add a connecting hamza at utterance onset; some instead pronounce sim or sum by moving the initial consonant.
rows.anchor: فإذا نطقوا بها مبتدئين زادوا همزة لئلا يقع ابتداؤهم بالساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ism is a noun with a deleted ending, originally sumw, derived from elevation because naming raises and publicizes the named one.
rows.anchor: وهو من الأسماء المحذوفة الأعجاز كيد ودم وأصله سمو بدليل تصريفه كأسماء وسمي وسميت واشتقاقه من السمو لأن التسمية تنويه بالمسمى وإشادة بذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word nabz for a nickname is related to nabr, raising the voice; nabz also names the outer peel of a palm tree.
rows.anchor: ومنه قيل للقب النبز من النبز بمعنى النبر وهو رفع الصوت والنبز قشر النخلة الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif in bism is omitted in writing because connected use is frequent; the lengthened bā compensates for it, and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz told his scribe to lengthen the bā.
rows.anchor: قد اتبعوا في حذفها حكم الدرج دون الابتداء الذي عليه وضع الخط لكثرة الاستعمال وقالوا طولت الباء تعويضا من طرح الألف وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه قال لكاتبه طول الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah derives from al-ilah; the generic word for a deity became specific to the true God, just as al-najm came to denote the Pleiades.
rows.anchor: و الله أصله الإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah, with its hamza deleted, is uniquely the name of the true God and is not used for another being; verbs meaning to deify derive from it.
rows.anchor: وأما ( الله ) بحذف الهمزة فمختص بالمعبود بالحق لم يطلق على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is a noun, not an adjective: it can be qualified but does not itself qualify an unspecified thing, and divine attributes require a named subject.
rows.anchor: بل اسم غير صفة ألا تراك تصفه ولا تصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also links Allah to aliha, to be bewildered: minds are dazed by trying to comprehend God, and lack of sound reflection lets error spread.
rows.anchor: وصيغة هذا الاسم وصيغة قولهم أله إذا تحير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says pronouncing Allah's lām emphatically is a sunnah; universal Arab practice shows it was inherited generation after generation.
rows.anchor: قد ذكر الزجاج ان تفخيمها سنة وعلى ذلك العرب كلهم وإطباقهم عليه دليل أنهم ورثوه كابرا عن كابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is the emphatic fa'lan form of mercy, while Rahim is fa'il; the former is more intensive, and added form signals added meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الرحمن ) من المبالغة ما ليس في ( الرحيم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman functions as an exclusive, established epithet for God, like Allah, and is not ordinarily used of anyone else.
rows.anchor: وهو من الصفات الغالبة كالدبران والعيوق والصعق لم يستعمل في غير الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Musaylima Rahman of Yamama, including in his poet's praise, is presented as a facet of the Banu Hanifa's unbelieving perversity.
rows.anchor: فباب من تعنتهم في كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman should be indeclinable by analogy with fa'lan adjectives such as عطشان and سكران, even though its divine specialization prevents a feminine form.
rows.anchor: أقيسه على أخواته من بابه أعني نحو عطشان وغرثان وسكران فلا أصرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy is figurative language for His beneficence: a kindly ruler does good to subjects, whereas harshness withholds favor.
rows.anchor: هو مجاز عن انعامه على عباده لأن الملك اذا عطف على رعيته ورق لهم أصابهم بمعروفه وإنعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He raises the question why the more emphatic attribute precedes the lesser when normal usage would progress from the lesser to the greater.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت فلم قدم ما هو أبلغ من الوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering is complementary: Rahman covers great and foundational blessings, and Rahim completes it by covering blessings that are delicate and subtle.
rows.anchor: فتناول جلائل النعم وعظائمها وأصولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd and madh both mean praising what is beautiful, whether a blessing or another merit; thanks, however, is only for a favor and uses heart, tongue, and limbs.
rows.anchor: الحمد والمدح أخوان وهو الثناء والنداء على الجميل من نعمة وغيرها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls praise the head of gratitude and says no servant thanks God without praising Him; al-Zamakhshari grades it weak.
rows.anchor: الحمد رأس الشكر ما شكر الله عبد لم يحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is the head of thanks because speaking of a blessing and praising its giver makes it more apparent than hidden belief or ambiguous bodily acts.
rows.anchor: لأن ذكر النعمة باللسان والثناء على موليها أشيع لها وأدل على مكانها من الاعتقاد وآداب الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is the opposite of blame and thanks the opposite of ingratitude; hamd is nominative as a subject with lillah as predicate, while some read it accusative with an implied verb.
rows.anchor: والحمد نقيضه الذم والشكر نقيضه الكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the nominative instead of an accusative verbal noun signals a stable, lasting meaning; he compares the construction with Abraham's raised response of peace.
rows.anchor: والعدل بها عن النصب إلى الرفع على الابتداء للدلالة على ثبات المعنى واستقراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's nominative response of peace indicates a more abiding greeting than the greeting he received, which was accusative.
rows.anchor: رفع السلام الثاني للدلالة على ان إبراهيم عليه السلام حياهم بتحية أحسن من تحيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that we praise God with praise; the next verse explains how, by saying that we worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: لأنه بيان لحمدهم له كأنه قيل كيف تحمدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article identifies the recognized kind of praise; those who take it as exhaustive of every possible praise are mistaken.
rows.anchor: هو نحو التعريف في أرسلها العراك وهو تعريف الجنس

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri reads al-hamdu with kasra on the dāl, assimilated to the following lām.
rows.anchor: بكسر الدال لاتباعها اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi Abla reads the lām of lillah with ḍamma by assimilation to the preceding dāl.
rows.anchor: بضم اللام لاتباعها الدال والذي جسرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers Ibrahim's reading because it makes the inflectional ending follow the stronger grammatical inflection, unlike al-Hasan's reading.
rows.anchor: وأشف القراءتين قراءة إبراهيم حيث جعل الحركة البنائية تابعة للاعرابية التي هي أقوى بخلاف قراءة الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb means owner; it can also be an intensive source used as an epithet, and unqualified Rabb is reserved for God while other uses require a possessive phrase.
rows.anchor: الرب المالك ومنه قول صفوان لأبي سفيان لأن يربني رجل من قريش أحب الي من ان يربني رجل من هوازن

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: The segment introduces Zayd ibn Ali reading rabb al-alamin as praise; the grammatical form and rationale continue in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb al-alamin may be accusative as praise, or governed by the omitted verb implied in praising God.
rows.anchor: بالنصب على المدح وقيل بما دل عليه الحمد لله كأنه قيل نحمد الله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-alamin means beings with knowledge, namely angels, humans, and jinn; another view includes all created bodies and accidents through which the Creator is known.
rows.anchor: العالم اسم لذوي العلم من الملائكة والثقلين وقيل كل ما علم به الخالق من الأجسام والأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural al-alamin encompasses every genus included by the word, and its rational masculine plural form is licensed by its implication of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ساغ ذلك لمعنى الوصفية فيه وهي الدلالة على معنى العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include malik, malik with a light lām, Abu Hanifa's verbal form with the day accusative, Abu Hurayra's accusative malik, and nominative malik or malik.
rows.anchor: قرىء ملك يوم الدين ومالك وملك بتخفيف اللام وقرأ أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه ملك يوم الدين بلفظ الفعل ونصب اليوم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reads malik in the accusative, while other readers take malik accusative as praise and some read malik in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه مالك بالنصب وقرأ غيره ملك وهو نصب على المدح ومنهم من قرأ مالك بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers malik because it is the reading of the two holy cities and agrees with Quranic language; kingship is broader, whereas ownership is more specific.
rows.anchor: ولأن الملك يعم والملك يخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-din is the day of recompense, as expressed by the proverb that one is repaid as one acts and a poetic example.
rows.anchor: ويوم الدين يوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle genitive used for present or future meaning is not a true possessive and cannot itself make a modifier definite.
rows.anchor: إذا أريد باسم الفاعل الحال أو الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle's genitive is definite when it conveys past meaning or a continuing state, so this phrase can modify the definite God; it may also mean king of affairs that day.
rows.anchor: فأما اذا قصد معنى الماضي كقولك هو مالك عبده أمس أو زمان مستمر كقولك زيد مالك العبيد كانت الاضافة حقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the whole affair on the Day of Judgment, as the declaration that dominion belongs to Him that day confirms.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون المعنى ملك الأمور يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's lordship, ownership, universal beneficence, and final authority show that none but He deserves praise and thanks.
rows.anchor: هذه الأوصاف التى أجريت على الله سبحانه من كونه ربا مالكا للعالمين لا يخرج منهم شيء من ملكوته وربوبيته

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and the verified grammarians treat the attached kāf, hā, and yā on iyya as markers of address, absence, or speech, not inflected pronouns.
rows.anchor: وليست بأسماء مضمرة وهو مذهب الأخفش وعليه المحققون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the object first expresses exclusivity: worship and the request for help are directed to God alone.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading has variants in the yā, hamza, and initial letter; Tufayl's verse witnesses the hā form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( إياك ) بتخفيف الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is the utmost submission and humility, reserved for God because He is the giver of the greatest blessings.
rows.anchor: والعبادة أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person praise to direct address is rhetorical iltifat; the explanation of its purpose continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: هذا يسمى الالتفات في علم البيان قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iltifat shifts among speech styles, as Quranic examples and Imru al-Qays's three successive shifts show; changing style renews attention and can carry special benefits.
rows.anchor: ولأن الكلام اذا نقل من أسلوب إلى أسلوب كان ذلك أحسن تطرية لنشاط السامع وايقاظا للإصغاء اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct address here makes the one already described as worthy of praise vivid, so worship and help are confined to the God whose qualities make Him deserving.
rows.anchor: فقيل إياك يا من هذه صفاته نخص بالعبادة والاستعانة لا نعبد غيرك ولا نستعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining worship with help unites what servants offer in drawing near to God with what they need from Him.
rows.anchor: ليجمع بين ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم وبين ما يطلبونه ويحتاجون اليه من جهته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship comes first because presenting a means before making a request makes a response more likely.
rows.anchor: لأن تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة ليستوجبوا الاجابة اليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for help is general, but its best sense is seeking God's aid and enabling grace to perform worship; the next verse specifies that request.
rows.anchor: والأحسن ان تراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for guidance explains the help being sought: when asked how He should assist, the servants answer, guide us to the straight path.
rows.anchor: بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة كأنه قيل كيف أعينكم فقالوا اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

rows.speaker: ابن حبيش
rows.claim: Ibn Hubaysh reads nasta'in with kasra on the initial nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن حبيش ( نستعين ) بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hada normally takes li or ila, but here it is used transitively like ikhtara; this pattern is illustrated by the choice of Moses's people.
rows.anchor: هدى أصله ان يتعدى باللام أو بإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for guidance despite already being guided means asking God for further guidance through special favor.
rows.anchor: ومعنى طلب الهداية وهم مهتدون طلب زيادة الهدى بمنح الإلطاف

rows.speaker: علي وأبي
rows.claim: Ali and Ubayy explain ihdina as keep us steadfast; the imperative and prayer share a request form and differ only in rank.
rows.anchor: وعن علي وأبي رضي الله عنهما اهدنا ثبتنا وصيغة الأمر والدعاء واحدة لأن كل واحد منهما طلب

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah reads the phrase as guide us rightly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله أرشدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat is the road, from a root meaning to swallow because it swallows up travelers; luqma has a similar sense.
rows.anchor: السراط الجادة من سرط الشيء اذا ابتلعه لأنه يسترط السابلة اذا سلكوه كما سمي لقما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat alternates sīn and ṣād because of the following ṭā; several readings exist, but pure ṣād is most eloquent, Qurashi, and the codex reading.
rows.anchor: والصراط من قلب السين صادا لأجل الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat has a plural and can be masculine or feminine; here it means the path of truth, the religion of Islam.
rows.anchor: ويجمع سرطا نحو كتاب وكتب ويذكر ويؤنث كالطريق والسبيل والمراد طريق الحق وهو ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an explanatory substitute for the straight path and virtually repeats the verb, emphasizing and identifying the straight way with the Muslims' way.
rows.anchor: بدل من الصراط المستقيم وهو في حكم تكرير العامل كأنه قيل اهدنا الصراط المستقيم اهدنا صراط الذين انعمت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated, first-general-then-specific description makes the believers a clear, emphatic example of those who possess the praised qualities.
rows.anchor: فائدته التوكيد لما فيه من التثنية والتكرير والإشعار بأن الطريق المستقيم بيانه وتفسيره صراط المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those blessed are believers, and the wording leaves blessing general because Islam gathers every blessing.
rows.anchor: والذين انعمت عليهم هم المؤمنون وأطلق الإنعام ليشمل كل إنعام لأن من أنعم عليه بنعمة الاسلام لم تبق نعمة الا أصابته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those blessed as Moses's companions before they changed their religion; another view identifies them as prophets.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هم أصحاب موسى قبل ان يغيروا وقيل هم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads the phrase as the path of those whom You blessed, using a relative pronoun instead of alladhina.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( صراط من انعمت عليهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr al-maghḍūb may substitute for those blessed, describing them as safe from anger and error, or qualify them as combining faith with safety from both.
rows.anchor: بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم على معنى ان المنعم عليهم هم الذين سلموا من غضب الله والضلال أو صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr can qualify the definite phrase because alladhina is not temporally delimited and the contrary identities of the two groups remove its ambiguity; it can also be accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: ولأن المغضوب عليهم والضالين خلاف المنعم عليهم فليس في غير إذا الإبهام الذي يأبى عليه ان يتعرف

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A circumstantial accusative reading of ghayr is attributed to the Prophet and Umar, and also reported from Ibn Kathir.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالنصب على الحال وهي قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب ورويت عن ابن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view identifies the angered as Jews, citing the verse that says God cursed them and was angry with them.
rows.anchor: وقيل المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's anger means His will to take vengeance on sinners, punish them, and treat them as a king does those under his authority.
rows.anchor: هو إرادة الانتقام من العصاة وإنزال العقوبة بهم وان يفعل بهم ما يفعله الملك اذا غضب على من تحت يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first عليهم is parsed as an object and the second as a subject.
rows.anchor: الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية والثانية محلها الرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative lā before astray is included because ghayr already carries a negative sense.
rows.anchor: لما في غير من معنى النفي كانه قيل لا المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي
rows.claim: Umar and Ali are reported to read wa-ghayr al-dallin, repeating the negative particle in a different construction.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما أنهما قرآ وغير الضالين

rows.speaker: أيوب السختياني
rows.claim: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reads al-dallin with hamza to avoid two adjacent silent consonants, as in dialect examples cited by Abu Zayd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني ( ولا الضألين ) بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin is an indeclinable sound used for the verb respond; it has long and short forms, and a poetic line illustrates it.
rows.anchor: آمين صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب كما ان رويد وحيهل وهلم أصوات سميت بها الأفعال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet explained Amin as meaning do it or answer.
rows.anchor:
وعن ابن عباس
4 سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel taught him Amin upon finishing al-Fatiha and called it like a seal on a book; it is not Quran because absent from the codices.
rows.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
5 ( لقنني جبريل عليه السلام آمين عند فراغي

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Hasan says the imam should not say Amin because he is the one supplicating; Abu Hanifa shares this view and is known to recite it quietly.
rows.anchor:
وعن الحسن لا يقولها الامام لأنه الداعي
وعن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله مثله والمشهور عنه وعن أصحابه انه يخفيها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Wail ibn Hujr reports that the Prophet said Amin aloud after reciting wa-la al-dallin.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان اذا قرأ ولا الضالين قال آمين ورفع بها صوته

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Ubayy ibn Ka'b that al-Fatiha has no equal in Torah, Gospel, or Quran and is the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Quran given to him.
rows.anchor:
وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بن كعب
7 ( ألا أخبرك بسورة لم ينزل في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن مثلها

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reports that God lifts an imminent calamity from a people for forty years after a child recites al-Fatiha and God hears it.
rows.anchor:
وعن حذيفة بن اليمان ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال
8 ( إن القوم ليبعث الله عليهم العذاب حتما مقضيا فيقرأ صبي من صبيانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To glorify God's name is to deny meanings unworthy of Him, such as compulsion or anthropomorphism; al-A'la means supremacy and power, not spatial height or literal settlement on the Throne.
rows.anchor: تنزيهه عما لا يصح فيه من المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A'la may qualify the Lord or the name, and Ali reads the verse as Glory to my Lord, the Most High.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه : سبحان ربي الأعلى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that after the command to glorify the Great Lord was revealed, worshippers were told to say it in bowing; after this verse, to say it in prostration.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( اجعلوها في ركوعكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything and formed it in an ordered, harmonious, well-fitted way, showing that it comes from a knowing and wise maker.
rows.anchor: أي خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه تسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God determined what benefits each animal and guided it to recognize how to use it; this is one example of God's vast guidance of humans and other creatures.
rows.anchor: فهداه إليه وعرفه وجه الانتفاع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote says a thousand-year-old blind snake finds fresh rue in a distant garden, rubs its eyes, and regains sight by God's permission.
rows.anchor: فربما كانت في برية بينها وبين الريف مسيرة أيام فتطوى تلك المسافة على طولها وعلى عماها حتى تهجم في بعض البساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance of human needs and of beasts, birds, and earth's creatures is too broad to be encompassed by description.
rows.anchor: وهدايات الله للإنسان إلى ما لا يحد من مصالحه وما لا يحصر من حوائجه في أغذيته وأدويته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading lightens the dāl in qaddara.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( قدر ) بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahwa can qualify the dried herbage: God grows pasture, then makes it dark withered chaff after its greenness; alternatively it describes the pasture as dark green before it becomes chaff.
rows.anchor: أخرج المرعى } أنبته { فجعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises the unlettered Prophet a clear sign: Gabriel recites revelation and he retains it, except what God abrogates by removing its ruling and recitation.
rows.anchor: أن يقرأ عليه جبريل ما يقرأ عليه من الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the Prophet hurried to repeat Gabriel's recitation, so he was told to wait for repeated instruction and would remember after any lapse.
rows.anchor: كان يعجل بالقراءة إذا لقنه جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may mean rare lapses: a report says he omitted a verse during prayer, and Ubayy thought it had been abrogated before the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
rows.anchor: أنه أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is a rhetorical affirmation of no forgetting, or the verse prohibits neglecting repeated recitation with an extra alif for rhyme; God may cause forgetting by abrogating recitation.
rows.anchor: الغرض نفى النسيان رأسا كما يقول الرجل لصاحبه أنت سهيمي فيما أملك إلا فيما شاء الله ولا يقصد استثناء شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knowing the loud and hidden may reassure the Prophet who recited aloud alongside Gabriel from fear of forgetting; alternatively it covers all hidden and public states and God's choices about what to erase or preserve.
rows.anchor: والله يعلم جهرك معه وما في نفسك مما يدعوك إلى الجهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuyassiruka coordinates with the promise of recitation, while the statement that God knows the loud and hidden is parenthetical; it means easing the Prophet toward memorizing revelation.
rows.anchor: معطوف على { سنقرئك } وقوله : { إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى } اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations are guidance to the easy, tolerant law or to the deeds leading to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل للشريعة السمحة التي هي أيسر الشرائع وأسهلها مأخذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had already exhausted his effort reminding them, while their defiance grieved him; the conditional means keep reminding after being charged to do so, as linked verses direct.
rows.anchor: قد استفرغ مجهوده في تذكيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively the apparent condition is a rebuke of the audience and signals that reminders will not affect their sealed hearts, as in the sarcastic example of preaching to tax collectors.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ظاهره شرطا ، ومعناه ذما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who fears God and a bad end will remember, reflect, and be led by thought to follow the truth.
rows.anchor: وينتفع بها { من يخشى } الله وسوء العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched who avoids the reminder is the unbeliever, or the most wicked unbeliever because of deep hostility toward the Messenger; some say the verse was revealed about al-Walid and Utba.
rows.anchor: الكافر ؛ لأنه أشقى من الفاسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says the passage was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Utba ibn Rabi'a.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وعتبة بن ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater fire may be the lowest layer of Hell, or Hell itself contrasted with the lesser fire of this world.
rows.anchor: السفلى من أطباق النار وقيل { الكبرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks a further degree of severity: the state between life and death is worse than burning, since the damned neither die to rest nor live usefully.
rows.anchor: لأن الترجح بين الحياة والموت أفظع من الصلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakka may mean cleansing oneself of polytheism and sins, purifying oneself for prayer, increasing in piety, or giving charity.
rows.anchor: أو تكثر من التقوى ، من الزكاة وهو النماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-salla may mean the five prayers; reports explain it as almsgiving and prayer, remembering one's return to God before praying, or remembering God on the way to the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: أي الصلوات الخمس ، نحو قوله : { ليس البر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets the successful person's purification as paying zakat al-fitr before going to the Eid prayer; he says he is content if his record contains no more than this proof.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه التصدق بصدقة الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, precedes and is not part of prayer, and may use any of God's names.
rows.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the worshipper remembers the return and standing before the Lord, then prays to Him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the person remembers God's name on the way to the prayer ground and performs the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك : وذكر اسم ربه في طريق المصلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing worldly life means failing to do what brings success; a variant uses third-person plural and Ibn Masud reads an explicit you plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يؤثرون ) على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This may refer to the teaching from success through the better, lasting Hereafter, or to the entire surah; its meaning is found in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله : { قد أفلح } إلى { أبقى }

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports asking the Prophet about scriptures; the reply counts 104, apportioned among Adam, Seth, Enoch, Abraham, and the four later named books.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه ( أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Abraham's scroll teaches a prudent person to guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his affairs.
rows.anchor: في صحف إبراهيم ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report promises ten rewards for each letter God revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad to whoever recites al-A'la.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله على إبراهيم وموسى ومحمد

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: When the Prophet recited this surah he said Glory to my Lord the Most High; Ali and Ibn Abbas are also reported to say it.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا قرأها قال : سبحان ربي الأعلى وكان علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says the Prophet liked this surah and reports that Michael was the first to say Glory to my Lord the Most High.
rows.anchor: أول من قال ( سبحان ربي الأعلى ) مكيائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghashiya is a calamity that envelops people in its terrors, meaning the Resurrection; another view identifies it as the Fire.
rows.anchor: الداهية التي تغشى الناس بشدائدها وتلبسهم أهوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humbled faces are laboring and exhausted in Hell, dragging chains and moving through fire; another view says they did evil in worldly life and now suffer, while another says their worldly effort brought no benefit.
rows.anchor: تعمل في النار عملا تتعب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the faces as monastic ascetics whose fasting and constant night prayer bring no reward in the next life.
rows.anchor: خشعت لله وعملت ونصبت في أعمالها من الصوم الدائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read as a reproachful insult, and tasla occurs with several vocalized or doubled readings.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( عاملة ناصبة ) على الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic term for being roasted applies to a sheep placed inside a pit of accumulated coals, not ordinary roasting over coals, a pan, or in an oven.
rows.anchor: أن يحفروا حفيرا فيجمعوا فيه جمرا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aniya means water at its utmost heat, as in the phrase between boiling water.
rows.anchor: متناهية في الحر ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dari is dried shibriq, a thorn camels graze while fresh but avoid once dry; Abu Dhu'ayb's poetry supplies examples of shibriq and dari'.
rows.anchor: الضريع يبيس الشبرق ، وهو جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difference from al-Haqqa's food of ghislin reflects the different kinds of punishment and classes of people: some eat zaqqum, some ghislin, and some dari'.
rows.anchor: العذاب ألوان ، والمعذبون طبقات ؛ فمنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La yusmin can describe the food or the thorn: it provides neither relief from hunger nor bodily strength; alternatively dari' is no food at all, just as sun is not shade.
rows.anchor: يعني : أن طعامهم من شيء ليس من مطاعم الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh claimed dari' fattened their camels; the response either denies this as a lie or says their food is a different, non-nourishing kind of thorn.
rows.anchor: قالت كفار قريش : إن الضريع لتسمن عليه إبلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed faces are radiant and beautiful, or enjoying luxury; they are pleased with their deeds after seeing the honor and reward those deeds bring.
rows.anchor: ذات بهجة وحسن ، كقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aliya describes a high place or elevated rank.
rows.anchor: عالية } من علو المكان أو المقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces, or the listener addressed, hear no futile speech; the word may denote idle speech, a speech marked by it, or a person who speaks idly, because Paradise's speech is wisdom and praise.
rows.anchor: لا يتكلم أهل الجنة إلا بالحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La tusma'u is also read in the passive with either ta or ya.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لا تسمع ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The running spring signifies an abundance of springs, as in the expression every soul knew.
rows.anchor: يريد عبونا في غاية الكثرة ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised couches may be elevated in rank or height, letting a believer see the kingdom granted by God; another view says they are stored away for them.
rows.anchor: مرفوعة } من رفعة المقدار أو السمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cups are already presented whenever wanted, or placed ready at the springs, or moderate in size between small and large.
rows.anchor: كلما أرادوها وجدوها موضوعة بين أيديهم عتيدة حاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cushions are lined up beside each other so that wherever one sits there is another to lean against.
rows.anchor: مساند ومطارح ، أينما أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarabi are broad, luxurious carpets, perhaps velvet rugs; they are spread out or scattered around the gathering places.
rows.anchor: وبسط عراض فاخرة . وقيل : هي الطنافس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking at camels is a call to reflection: their design shows deliberate governance, with knees suited to loading, strength for distant burdens, docility, and tall necks.
rows.anchor: حيث خلقها للنهوض بالأثقال وجرها إلى البلاد الشاحطة فجعلها تبرك حتى تحمل عن قرب ويسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise man unfamiliar with camels inferred their long necks from the account of their remarkable design; they endure long droughts and eat plants other animals avoid.
rows.anchor: وحين أراد بها أن تكون سفائن البر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the judge Shurayh told him he was going to look at how camels were created.
rows.anchor: قال : لقيت شريحا القاضي فقلت : أين تريد ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels fit naturally alongside sky, mountains, and earth because these are the objects Arabs observe in their valleys and deserts; cloud is not actually a name for camels, though poetry compares them.
rows.anchor: قد انتظم هذه الأشياء نظر العرب في أوديتهم وبواديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky has been raised to great height without support or pillars.
rows.anchor: رفعا بعيد المدى بلا مساك وبغير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are set firmly in place and do not lean or move.
rows.anchor: نصبا ثابتا ، فهي راسخة لا تميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth has been flattened, leveled, and made a resting place for those who move across it.
rows.anchor: سطحا بتمهيد وتوطئة ، فهي مهاد للمتقلب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali reads all four verbs as first-person active forms, with the object omitted; Harun al-Rashid reads sataht with doubling.
rows.anchor: على البناء للفاعل وتاء الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These created things testify to the Creator's power, including His power to resurrect; people should heed the Messenger's warning and prepare for meeting God.
rows.anchor: هذه المخلوقات الشاهدة على قدرة الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's duty is to remind, as in the declaration that he is responsible only for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { إن عليك إلا البلاغ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaytir means one who dominates or compels them; the word is open-ta in the dialect of Tamim and may take an object there.
rows.anchor: بمتسلط ، كقوله : { وما أنت عليهم بجبار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be disconnected: the Prophet cannot control them, but God has power over those who turn away and disbelieve; another parsing attaches it to the command to remind only those whose faith he still hopes for.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع ، أي : لست بمستول عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akbar is the greater torment of Hell; a reading adds the pronoun fa-innahu before God will punish him, while Abu Ja'far lengthens iyabihim and offers two derivations.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود ( فإنه يعذبه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the return and accounting phrases intensifies the warning: they return only to the all-powerful God, who alone is responsible for accounting every tiny thing.
rows.anchor: معناه التشديد في الوعيد ، وأن إيابهم ليس إلا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever recites Surat al-Ghashiya will be given an easy reckoning by God.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الغاشية حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Fajr is Meccan; the source gives its length as thirty verses, with an alternative count of twenty-nine, and says it followed Surat al-Layl.
rows.anchor: مكية ، وآياتها 30 وقيل 29

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first Ad were descendants of Ad son of Aws son of Iram son of Sam; the earliest were called Ad al-Ula or Iram after their ancestor, and later people were Ad al-Akhira.
rows.anchor: لعقب عاد بن عوص بن إرم بن سام بن نوح عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram may be an appositive identifying the ancient Ad, or the name of their town and land; Ibn al-Zubayr reads it as a possessive construction meaning the people of Iram.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان لعاد ، وإيذان

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير والحسن
rows.claim: Readings include Ibn al-Zubayr's possessive Iram, Hasan's open forms, a lightened r, and a possessive construction with Dhat al-Imad.
rows.anchor: قراءة ابن الزبير ( بعاد إرم ) على الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhat al-Imad can mean Ad's lofty city, people dwelling in tents or tall as pillars, or a city with pillars; Iram may itself be a landmark or a city-name.
rows.anchor: يعني : بعاد أهل أعلام ذات العماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long report says Shaddad ruled the world and, after hearing of Paradise, built a city of gold, silver, jewels, trees, and rivers over three hundred years; God destroyed his people before they arrived.
rows.anchor: فسمع بذكر الجنة فقال أبني مثلها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن قلابة
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Qilaba says he found the city while searching for camels, took what he could, and later described it to Mu'awiya; Ka'b matched him to a prophecy of its discoverer.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن قلابة : أنه خرج في طلب إبل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La yukhlaq mithluha may compare the physical scale and strength of the Ad, whose men were said to be four hundred cubits tall, or the uniqueness of Shaddad's city; Ibn al-Zubayr has another reading.
rows.anchor: عظم أجرام وقوة ، كان طول الرجل منهم أربعمائة ذراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabou al-sakhr means they cut mountain rock and made homes in it; another report says Thamud first carved mountains and built 1,700 stone cities.
rows.anchor: قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's title Dhu al-Awtad may refer to his numerous forces and camp stakes, or to torture by stakes as inflicted on the hairdresser of his daughter and Asiya.
rows.anchor: لكثرة جنوده ومضاربهم التي كانوا يضربونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhina taghaw is best parsed as an accusative of blame; it can also be nominative or genitive as a modifier of Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: أو مجرورا على وصف المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning a whip makes the punishment in this life seem small beside what awaits in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن ما أحله بهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبيد
rows.claim: Umar ibn Ubayd says al-Hasan would comment that God has many whips and seized the wrongdoers with one of them.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبيد : كان الحسن إذا أتى على هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mirsad is a place where watchers wait, formed like miqat from waqt; it figuratively says God lies in wait with punishment and wrongdoers cannot escape.
rows.anchor: المكان الذي يترتب فيه الرصد

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: When asked where God is, an Arab answered that He is at the ambush.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العرب أنه قيل له : أين ربك ؟ فقال : بالمرصاد

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd recited this surah before a tyrant, addressed him as one threatened by God's watchfulness, and was praised for confronting rulers and innovators with argument.
rows.anchor: وعن عمرو بن عبيد رحمه الله أنه قرأ هذه السورة عند بعض الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human passage connects to God's lying in wait: God seeks obedience and final success and has punishment ready for the disobedient, whereas people care only for immediate pleasures.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يريد من الإنسان إلا الطاعة والسعي للعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses are syntactically balanced by an understood pronoun before the second condition; the first fa-yaqulu is the predicate of al-insan, with the intervening time clause delayed.
rows.anchor: وأما هو إذا ما ابتلاه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both abundance and restriction are tests: abundance tests gratitude against denial, and restriction tests patience against despair, as the verse about testing with good and evil confirms.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's withholding is not humiliation; failing to grant a favor is an absence of generosity, not an insult, just as not receiving a gift is not being insulted.
rows.anchor: الإخلال بالتفضل لا يكون إهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first rebuke may target the claim that wealth proves deserved honor: God gives freely, with piety rather than ancestry or status as the relevant criterion.
rows.anchor: لأنه قال على قصد خلاف ما صححه الله عليه وأثبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the rebuke also targets calling a lack of new gifts humiliation, despite acknowledging God's prior favors; not receiving generosity is not being demeaned.
rows.anchor: أن ينساق الإنكار والذم إلى قوله : { ربى أهانن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qira'at include a light or doubled dāl in qaddara; at pause, the final nūn is still and the yā is omitted, with its kasra retained in connected speech.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( فقدر ) بالتخفيف والتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes the human claim, then points to worse behavior: people fail to care for orphans or encourage feeding the poor while enjoying wealth.
rows.anchor: ردع للإنسان عن قوله : ثم قال : بل هناك شر من القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The encouragement phrase has a variant with yā or tā; Ibn Masud reads the tā with ḍamma as mutual encouragement.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( يكرمون ) وما بعده بالياء والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akla lamma means a combined, indiscriminate eating of lawful and unlawful wealth; a line by al-Hutay'a witnesses the use of lamma.
rows.anchor: ذا لم وهو الجمع بين الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heirs may combine their inheritance with others' shares; one view says women and children were disinherited and their property consumed along with the men's shares.
rows.anchor: يعني : أنهم يجمعون في أكلهم بين نصيبهم من الميراث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says heirs knowingly mix their own lawful inheritance with property the deceased had obtained through wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يأكلون ما جمعه الميت من الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse condemns heirs who acquire wealth easily and squander it on indulgent quantities and varieties of food, drink, and fruit.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يذم الوارث الذي ظفر بالمال سهلا مهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hubb jamma is abundant, intense love of money marked by greed and withholding the rights due from it.
rows.anchor: كثيرا شديدا مع الحرص والشره ومنع الحقوق
